ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the figure, smooth parallel metal guide rails are fixed on a horizontal plane, the left ends are connected by a wire, and a conducting rod is placed perpendicularly and at rest on the guide rails to form a circuit. Under the action of an external force F, the bar magnet above the circuit moves vertically upward at a uniform speed. During the uniform-speed motion, the external force F does work WF, the magnetic field force does work W1 on the conducting rod, the magnet does work W2 against the magnetic field force, gravity does work WG on the magnet, the Joule heat generated in the circuit is Q, and the kinetic energy obtained by the conducting rod is Ek. Then (　　)

Under the action of an external force F, the bar magnet above the circuit moves vertically upward at a uniform speed. During this uniform-speed motion, what relationship is satisfied among the work W2 done by the magnet against the magnetic field force, the work W1 done by the magnetic field force on the conducting rod, and the Joule heat Q generated in the circuit?

ready2_open_rewrite.resolved_question_text: As shown in the figure, smooth parallel metal guide rails are fixed on a horizontal plane, the left ends are connected by a wire, and a conducting rod is placed perpendicularly and at rest on the guide rails to form a circuit. Under the action of an external force F, the bar magnet above the circuit moves vertically upward at a uniform speed. During this uniform-speed motion, what relationship is satisfied among the work W2 done by the magnet against the magnetic field force, the work W1 done by the magnetic field force on the conducting rod, and the Joule heat Q generated in the circuit?
ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: In the figure there are two parallel metal guide rails fixed on a horizontal plane, and the left ends are connected by a wire to form a closed circuit; on the right side there is a conducting rod spanning the two guide rails and able to move along the guide rails. Above the circuit there is a vertically placed bar magnet, the upper end of the magnet is marked S and the lower end is marked N, and above the magnet a vertically upward external force F is drawn, indicating that the magnet is pulled upward at a uniform speed. Reasoning: When the magnet moves upward away from the guide-rail circuit, the magnetic flux passing through the circuit changes, and an induced current is produced in the circuit. The magnetic field produced by the induced current will hinder the relative motion between the magnet and the circuit, so the magnet is subjected to a downward magnetic field resistance; the magnet does work W2 against this magnetic field force, and this part of the work is energy input into the induced current and conducting-rod system. When the induced current flows through the conducting rod, the conducting rod is subjected to an Ampere force in the magnetic field, and the magnetic field force does work W1 on the conducting rod, causing the conducting rod to obtain mechanical energy; at the same time the circuit has resistance, and the current passing through the circuit produces Joule heat Q. The guide rails are smooth, and other net changes in energy storage are neglected, so the input energy equals the sum of the increase in mechanical energy of the conducting rod and the Joule heat, that is, W2=W1+Q. Therefore the relationship among the three is W2-W1=Q.
